children.value: ; its time and communication latency are unmeasured. The clean zero input is assumed, with initialization timing/faults excluded. The parent chapter’s conditional surface-code reports specify code distances, factories, hardware error rates and complete serial workloads. A raw RX count or constant logical depth does not determine physical qubits or runtime.

QDK’s arbitrary-rotation cost is an empirical mean-fit model. It does not supply a concrete Clifford+T approximation or certified output-error bound. The synthesis-bias allocation is therefore conditional on the model scalar bounding output-distribution variation. No certified overall output-confidence statement follows from that assumption. The
supplies reporting conventions and hardware profiles, not physical counts for this walk.

Checks retain complex amplitudes, global phases, nonzero starting vertices, negative couplings/times, normalized versus unnormalized time conventions, final measurement maps, and lowering equivalence. Uniformity, antipodal transfer, periodicity and dense adjacency structure have independent references. A deliberately disagreeing reference is rejected by the checker. Results must meet a declared
numerical tolerance before they are labeled checked.

No Lean formalization is integrated for this implementation. The factorization above is a mathematical explanation; a proof artifact would need a reproduced toolchain, theorem assumptions and an explicit circuit connection. General continuous-time graph walks additionally require implemented graph access and approximation analysis; they are not supplied by this hypercube circuit.
The implementation uses original MIT code with
), NumPy and SciPy. Exact build versions, source hashes and circuit digests accompany the generated artifacts.
explains unitary time evolution. It supports the Hamiltonian viewpoint rather than validating this walk implementation or its resource estimate.
